scope: Local functional and automated acceptance of shared protection capacity, progress and public IP switches

environment.engine: Real rules-only Rust gRPC services; NER disabled
environment.provider: Controlled local HTTP provider; no real provider account or API key
environment.dependencies: Real isolated PostgreSQL, Redis, Keycloak and Mailpit pilot fixtures
environment.replica_scope: The extra gateway shares the real Redis queue and Rust engine; local application/operator metadata is ephemeral per gateway, so this is not acceptance of production load-balanced identity storage.

enterprise_go.skip_reason: External opt-in checks are outside this queue change and were not counted as passes.

verification.shared_core: Native functional tests, type checks, package build/update, immutable version conflicts, rollback and both consumer integrity checks passed.
verification.compose_configuration: Both backend Compose configurations validated without printing secrets.

observed_contracts: Separate gateway processes share real Redis FIFO: positions 1 and 2 update after cancellation, and the next job acquires the single configured slot.
Concurrent real Redis admissions enforce combined running and waiting limits; independent core namespaces remain available.
Community inspection, protected chat and authenticated embeddings share protection capacity; expired/cancelled waiters do not later dispatch.
Both real frontends display server queue position and processing over the original POST, cancel queued work and complete a fresh restored reply.
Unauthorized, role/model/tenant/quota denied and security-blocked requests do not reach a provider.
All three providers retain JSON and native SSE restoration, including repeated/split placeholders, cancellation and next-request recovery.
Full queue, wait timeout, processing deadline, lost Pub/Sub notification, owner expiry and shutdown during admission fail safely.

Stopping the owned Redis container rejects new protection work with 503 queue_unavailable and terminates queued/running work without dispatching the waiter. After all in-flight work drains, restarting Redis permits a fresh restored reply.

The fault run exposed stale lease cleanup after an unavailable Redis removal. Bounded opaque cleanup tickets and batched reconciliation corrected the recovery delay; the repeated real outage test passed.
Daily/minute-IP switch combinations, development daily exemption and preserved public global/core capacity were verified.
Split UTF-8/CRLF, malformed/oversized/truncated progress, aborts, ordinary JSON fallback and stream=true incompatibility were checked.
acceptance_limits: No hosted ingress, production sizing, buffering/timeouts or cost measurement was performed.
Installed Chrome/Edge manual acceptance was not rerun for this feature. New C29/E41 rows remain NOT RUN; earlier manual rows keep their recorded scope.
Real provider credentials, external SMTP/domain tests and long NER quality/performance runs were outside this work.
CI's required-boundary list was extended to eight; this local run did not execute the model-download/standalone CI bootstrap or publish a CI run.
A dead gateway still relies on bounded Redis leases; Redis state loss requires verified drain or the documented quiescence horizon.

cleanup.native_processes: Owned pilot process tree and Playwright web servers stopped; owned gateway, engine, provider and frontend ports verified closed.
cleanup.docker: The four pilot containers were returned to their initial stopped state; no Docker containers remain running.
cleanup.preserved: Existing database volumes, private fixture files, user provider credentials and browser sessions were preserved. No Git staging, commit, push or deployment was performed.
